tagline: Home of the Buddha's Footprint, Muak Lek milk, and waterfalls at the foot of Khao Yai
introHtml:
Saraburi is a town most people drive straight through on the way up to Isan, but there's actually plenty here. The first thing that comes to mind is Wat Phra Phutthabat Ratchaworamahawihan, which enshrines a revered footprint of the Buddha. Around the third lunar month it hosts the flower offering ceremony, where people carry khao phansa flowers and place them in the alms bowls of monks walking up to the temple — a sight you'll only catch here.

Out toward Muak Lek and Kaeng Khoi, in the hills below Khao Yai, there are so many dairy farms that the area is known as milk country. You can stop along the way for fresh milk, ice cream, and farm products. Muak Lek Waterfall and Chet Sao Noi Waterfall are popular spots to cool off in the water. As for food, there's everything from milk and farm goods to Sao Hai curry puffs, sticky rice with coconut, and street food at the markets in town.
bestTime: November–February, when the weather is cool and pleasant for the hills below Khao Yai and the Muak Lek farms. The flower offering ceremony at Phra Phutthabat falls on the start of Buddhist Lent, around July.

highlights.name: Wat Phra Phutthabat Ratchaworamahawihan
highlights.blurb: The town's landmark temple, enshrining a footprint of the Buddha. People come specifically to pay respects and see the beautiful gilded mondop — it's the first thing most people picture when they think of Saraburi.

highlights.name: Flower Offering Ceremony (Tak Bat Dok Mai)
highlights.blurb: A Buddhist Lent tradition where people hold khao phansa flowers and place them in the alms bowls of monks walking up to Wat Phra Phutthabat. The path fills with purple and yellow blooms — a scene you can only see here.

highlights.name: Muak Lek milk country
highlights.blurb: Muak Lek district has so many dairy farms it's earned the name milk country. Stop along the way to try fresh milk, ice cream, and farm products.

highlights.name: Waterfalls below Khao Yai
highlights.blurb: Muak Lek Waterfall and Chet Sao Noi Waterfall sit on the side next to Khao Yai. The water is clear and swimmable — a favorite place for locals to cool off.

highlights.name: Sunflower fields and hillside farms
highlights.blurb: From late rainy season into early winter, sunflower fields bloom around Phra Phutthabat and Wang Muang — a handy spot to stop for photos along the way.

highlights.name: Pa Sak Jolasid Dam at Wang Muang
highlights.blurb: The Pa Sak reservoir stretches all the way to Wang Muang district, with wide waterside viewpoints to stop, rest, and take photos.

foodScene.name: Fresh milk and Muak Lek farm products
foodScene.note: Dairy farms around Muak Lek sell fresh milk, yogurt, and milk ice cream right at the farm. Stop for a taste on the spot or grab some to take home.

foodScene.name: Sao Hai curry puffs (kari pap)
foodScene.note: A specialty from Sao Hai district — crisp pastry with generous fillings, both savory and sweet. A favorite gift people pick up on the way through.

foodScene.name: Sticky rice with coconut and local sweets
foodScene.note: Markets in town sell sticky rice with coconut topped various ways, alongside traditional Thai sweets — easy snacks to grab while you're out.

foodScene.name: Noodles and street food in town
foodScene.note: The market areas in Saraburi town have noodle shops and walk-and-eat snacks at local prices, with plenty of stalls to choose from.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laab are easy to find all over town — bold flavors and an easy meal, with lots of places serving it.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot)
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with plenty of spots to choose from at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Hillside cafes around Muak Lek
foodScene.note: The road up to Muak Lek and the edge of Khao Yai has cafes with mountain views — a good place to sip coffee in the cool air between waterfall stops.

foodScene.name: Freshwater fish and riverside restaurants
foodScene.note: Restaurants along the Pa Sak River and by the dam serve fresh freshwater fish, eaten with a view over the wide water.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Phutthabat Ratchaworamahawihan
attractions.blurb: An important temple enshrining a footprint of the Buddha, with a beautiful gilded mondop. People come to pay respects all year round.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Phutthachai
attractions.blurb: A temple at the foot of a hill where an image of the Buddha appears on the cliff face, along with a footprint of the Buddha and ancient rock paintings.

attractions.name: Muak Lek Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A waterfall below Khao Yai that flows down in tiers. The water is clear and swimmable — a popular spot for locals around Muak Lek to cool off.

attractions.name: Chet Sao Noi Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tier waterfall in the Muak Lek area, with pools to swim in and tube down — great to visit as a group.

attractions.name: Muak Lek dairy farm
attractions.blurb: Dairy farms around Muak Lek open for visits, where you can feed the calves and buy fresh milk and ice cream from the farm — good for bringing kids.

attractions.name: Chet Sao Noi Waterfall National Park
attractions.blurb: Forested land in the hills below Khao Yai with streams and waterfalls — good for shady nature walks and camping overnight.

attractions.name: Phra Phutthabat sunflower fields
attractions.blurb: Sunflower fields bloom yellow from late rainy season into early winter around Phra Phutthabat district — a popular photo spot.

attractions.name: Saraburi old town and markets
attractions.blurb: The town center has markets and local food shops to graze through, before or after heading up to the hills.
